description: Source (sending) visual cortical area; row label in the printed matrix. 3 labels (PIT, CIT, STP) are row-only -- they appear as 'From' areas but have no matching 'To' column in the printed table.
Target (receiving) visual cortical area; column label in the printed matrix.
The symbol printed in that matrix cell, verbatim.
notes: large vs. small '+' (evidence tier) is NOT distinguishable in this column -- see evidence_tier

description: TRUE for the 32 diagonal cells (from_area == to_area) representing intrinsic within-area circuitry, which the paper explicitly excludes from the tabulated pathways.

Recoded presence/absence of an interareal pathway. 1 = pathway reported ('+' of either evidence tier); 0 = pathway explicitly tested and found absent ('.' dot, or 'NR'/'NR?' nonreciprocal-absent); NA = not carefully tested for (blank), existence uncertain ('?'), or intrinsic diagonal cell.
notes: not an effect strength, presence/absence only

description: For connection_code==1 only: whether the pathway was reported in >=1 full-length manuscript ('manuscript', printed as a large '+'), only in an abstract/unpublished study ('abstract_or_unpublished', small '+'), or whether the PDF text layer did not capture this specific '+' character so size could not be determined from font metrics ('unresolved', recovered via pixel-darkness cross-check -- 17 of 286 '+' cells).
source_location: derived from the printed '+' font size in the PDF text layer

description: TRUE for '?' and 'NR?' cells: the paper flags the pathway's existence (or its nonreciprocal absence) as uncertain owing to conflicting reports in the literature.
TRUE for 'NR'/'NR?' cells: the pathway is absent in this specific direction even though the reciprocal (opposite-direction) connection has been reported.
